title: needs-decision: main-session (non-delegated) wake-up-discipline stalls are outside #2624's delegation-mechanism fix
body:
## Background

kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221 (closed, evidence-accumulation issue) recorded a wake-up-discipline stall pattern across several session shapes and asked which direction was worth pursuing next. Its 2026-08-31 comment records a distinct sub-shape that the decision recorded on that issue does not reach:

> A 2026-08-30/31 session on this repository hit the same failure three times in a **main, non-delegated session** — one that had read the current instructions directly rather than through a delegation brief. [...] The three occurrences:
>
> 1. After committing one of four planned commits, reported progress and ended the turn. The operator asked "are you working in the background or stopped?"
> 2. Immediately after the same question was answered, reported again on the next milestone and stopped. The operator asked a second time.
> 3. Stated "I will wait for CI and then start the quiet window" and ended the turn **without arming any wait**. Two review findings had already landed; they went unnoticed for **3.6 hours** until the operator reported them.
>
> Occurrence 3 matters most [...] There was **no background task to be mistaken about**. [...] The distinguishing feature across all three was that the session had just produced a **reportable milestone**. Reporting appears to act as a turn-completion signal on its own, independent of any belief about resumption.

(Refs `#2179`, `#2210`; observed on PR `#2325` and PR `#2330`.)

kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221 drew two conclusions directly relevant here:

- "Wording aimed at delegation briefs cannot reach this surface. A main session never reads a delegation brief. If the countermeasure stays in that layer, this variant is out of its scope by construction."
- "A mechanical signal did work. Once the session began ending each turn with an actually-armed background wait whose completion re-invoked it, the stalls stopped. [...] That is a structural fix rather than a wording one."

kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221's own decision (2026-09-05) chose to investigate a *delegation-mechanism* direction instead (preferring a non-context-inheriting subagent for full worker delegation), filed as kurone-kito/idd-skill#2624. kurone-kito/idd-skill#2624's own investigation (see its evidence-table comment) confirms this main-session shape is explicitly outside that direction's reach: no delegation occurs in a main session at all, so there is no context-inheriting-vs-non-inheriting choice to make there. This issue exists to record that residual gap and open the question of what (if anything) closes it, per kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221's own template ("A chosen direction is recorded [...] and any resulting concrete follow-up work is filed as its own separate issue").

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision among the options below, not a pre-selected direction.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Require every main-session turn-ending "will do X" style statement to be paired with an actually-armed background wait.** kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221's own comment 3 reports this mechanical signal worked reliably once adopted in that session: every subsequent phase transition was driven by a completion notification rather than the session simply deciding to continue. This would need to be expressed as a constraint on the main session's own turn-ending behavior (e.g. in `idd-ci.instructions.md`'s Wake-up discipline section, currently framed around delegated workers and CI/advisory waits specifically), not the delegation-brief layer kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221 already found to be out of reach for this shape.
2. **Treat this as a Claude-Code-product/harness-level constraint outside idd-skill's own instruction-file reach.** An instruction file can ask a session to end every turn on an armed wait, but cannot mechanically prevent a session from asserting a future-tense claim ("I will check now") and stopping anyway — enforcing that may require a runtime-level constraint on what a session's own final-turn state is allowed to claim, which is out of scope for a documentation-only fix. If chosen, record explicitly which part (if any) instruction wording can still reinforce, and route the runtime-level part to a separate product-feedback channel rather than an idd-skill instruction change.
3. **Do nothing — accept the risk as inherent to a main session's own judgment about when a turn is "done."** Worth stating as the explicit status-quo option: the pattern is real but session-severity-dependent (occurrence 3's 3.6-hour blind spot was the most costly observed instance), and a maintainer may judge further instruction-file reinforcement is not worth the added prose weight against three observed occurrences in one session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A chosen direction is recorded (as a comment or an update to this issue) among the options above, or an equivalent alternative a maintainer proposes instead.
- [ ] Any resulting concrete follow-up work (an instruction-file change, a separate product-feedback report, or an explicit accept-the-risk note) is filed as its own issue or report referencing this one, rather than implemented directly here.
- [ ] This issue is closed once the direction is recorded, per kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221's own closure criterion.

## Scope notes for whoever picks this up

- This is a decision issue, not directly autonomously actionable — similar in spirit and autopilot-suitability tier to kurone-kito/idd-skill#2221 itself.
- Do not conflate this with kurone-kito/idd-skill#2624's own scope: that issue is specifically about the *delegation-mechanism* choice for delegated workers, already decided and landed; this issue is about a main, non-delegated session's own turn-ending behavior, which #2624's own investigation confirmed is a structurally different surface.
- This issue's own drafting and publication did not follow the full owner-marker/publication-token ceremony described in `docs/issue-authoring-skill.md`'s "Authoring label lifecycle" section — this repository has no designated authoring journal target configured (`.github/idd/config.json` has no `issueAuthoring.journal` field), matching the same disclosed simplification kurone-kito/idd-skill#2606 already established as this repository's operative practice (that issue's own decided follow-up, kurone-kito/idd-skill#2621, addresses making the ceremony mechanically enforced instead of prose-only). Published directly under the `status:needs-decision` label with a fresh duplicate-check immediately before creation.
